text.text_excerpt: This is a separate entity of the Lafitte Guest House but is inside of the hotel. Apparently they have some sort of contract with the bar (the actual Lafitte Blacksmith Bar across the street) and serve the awesome purple drink of the Lafitte Blacksmith Bar. They have a full bar inside of the boutique hotel, complete with flatscreens and a really awesome decor and furniture. I suggest to people that aren't going to the Lafitte Blacksmith Bar for the history but only for the booze, to come here. It's the same price without the crowd.

Had a delightful time here for a fraction of the price of the nearby Hampton Inn. Rooms are clean and comfortable, although yes, you have to be a bit of a contortionist to use the toilet in the extremely small old-timey bathrooms. I loved the communal kitchen--it was well stocked with snacks and the morning coffee and toast were delightful either on the balcony or back in the room. As other have said, yes, you're on Bourbon Street, but the quiet end, far from the vomiting masses. There's a classic bar, 24 hour diner steps away, and you're close to all the major attractions. A really great stay.

We stayed at Lafitte Guest House the weekend after Christmas. Overall, we enjoyed our stay and would very likely return -- if they get the wifi issue fixed. We had rooms 40 and 33; 40 is the attic room and perfect for a family with children. There were two beds in there and plenty of room to drop an air mattress (or two!) if you needed. Here are some random thoughts in no particular order: LOCATION: brilliant. At the "quieter" end of Bourbon Street. Everything is within walking distance .. French Market 5 minutes, Jackson Square 10 minutes. Probably an excellent place to book during Mardis Gras, though like everywhere else the rack rates double.
